title: Do two discounts add up?
hook: 20% off, then 10% off: is that a 30% price cut?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate sequential discounts from the reduced base.

objective: Calculate sequential discounts from the reduced base.

claims.text: A applies 20% off and then 10% off the reduced price. B applies 30% off once. Scaled model; fictional offers; no other fees.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Original=100€, A=€72 and B=€70. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.8,0.9]; B=["*","x",0.7]; x denotes Original. At x=100, A=72, B=70. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The second percentage acts on what remains. Multiplying 0.8 by 0.9 leaves 0.72 of the original price, not 0.70. The changed base explains the gap on the receipts.

claims.text: A fictional €200 item gets 20% off, then 10% off the reduced price. What is the final price? Correct: €144. The second discount acts on €160, leaving 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72 of €200, not 0.70.
